cover.tagline: One spell in, five spells out — a goblin horde that casts itself.
cover.identity: Zada, Hedron Grinder turns every cheap spell that targets only her into a copy for each other creature you control — so a one-mana cantrip aimed at your commander becomes a fistful of cards when the Goblins are out in force. You flood the board with token makers, fuel monster turns with rituals like Battle Hymn and Brightstone Ritual, and convert the frenzy into damage through Impact Tremors, storm payoffs like Grapeshot and Empty the Warrens, and sacrifice engines like Goblin Bombardment. It plays like a tribal aggro deck that suddenly combusts into a storm deck.

how_it_wins:
Everything starts with bodies, and you are never short of bodies. Dragon Fodder, Krenko's Command, Mogg War Marshal, Empty the Warrens, Siege-Gang Commander, and the attack-trigger crew — General Kreat, Searslicer Goblin, Howlsquad Heavy — flood the table fast, and Krenko, Mob Boss doubles the count every time he taps. Know exactly what Krenko is: verified line 004 shows that under Goblin Warchief he costs {1}{R}{R}, activates the turn he lands, and turns five Goblins into ten — but the database's promised infinite Krenko/Prospector loop does not exist in this deck, because Krenko is not your commander and stays tapped after his one activation. He is a burst, and a very good one — play him like it.

A wide board is not just an army here; it is the multiplier on everything else, and Zada, Hedron Grinder is the machine doing the multiplying. Line 001 shows the verified floor: one Crimson Wisps with four Goblin tokens out draws you five cards and hastes the team for one red mana. Expedite, Renegade Tactics, Ancestors' Aid, and Fists of Flame all fit the same slot, and line 003 proves that slot's ceiling — Fists of Flame copies resolving in sequence, each drawing before it buffs, add up to 32 power of trample off a board of 1/1s. Storm-Kiln Artist gets paid a Treasure for every spell you cast or copy, and Reliquary Tower lets you keep everything you drew.

The mana comes from rituals that scale with your board and the table: Battle Hymn, Brightstone Ritual, Skirk Prospector (verified in line 004 as a true mana ability — no stack, no responses, usable mid-payment), Mana Geyser, and Seething Song, discounted by Ruby Medallion and Goblin Warchief. Line 002 gives you the storm math to spend it on: copies are put on the stack, not cast, so an Empty the Warrens as your fourth spell makes eight Goblins and eight Impact Tremors damage to each opponent, while a later Grapeshot counts only your real casts. Count your casts, not your resolutions.

The ceiling is a verified true infinite. Line 005 proves that Haze of Rage with buyback plus Storm-Kiln Artist goes mana-positive once three spells have been cast — each recast returns the card to hand, mints more Treasures than the next cast costs, and pumps the whole team another +1/+0 per copy, without bound; two casts already leave nine Treasures and a 20/2 Storm-Kiln Artist. From there you assemble the kill yourself: trample via Fists of Flame, tokens-into-Tremors via Empty the Warrens off the Treasure mana, or a Grapeshot riding the storm count the loop keeps raising. And if the first wave breaks early, you rebuild — Past in Flames and Faithless Looting recycle the chain, Goblin Dark-Dwellers rebuys a cheap spell, and Goblin Matron and Moggcatcher find the missing piece.

combo_lines.001: Open the casebook on the clause this whole deck is built around: when Zada, Hedron Grinder's ability resolves, the copies are put on the stack — they are not cast. That one distinction decides everything downstream: Zada does not re-trigger on her own copies, and they add nothing to your storm count. The facts before the court, verified against the comprehensive rules (June 19, 2026 update): Zada, four Goblin tokens, one red mana, Crimson Wisps in hand, the spell cast targeting only her — four copies join the original, each aimed at a different Goblin, and each resolves in full, draw and buff alike. The holding, for one mana and one card: five cards drawn, five red creatures with haste until end of turn. Every one-target cantrip in the deck follows this blueprint; carry it to the table.
combo_lines.002:
Storm is a trigger on casting, and it counts only the spells cast before its spell that turn — the copies it makes are put on the stack, not cast. Apply that to the facts, verified against the comprehensive rules (June 19, 2026 update): Impact Tremors on your battlefield, four Mountains, and Battle Hymn, Brightstone Ritual, and Dragon Fodder already cast when Empty the Warrens arrives as the fourth spell. Storm sees three, so three copies join the original; four resolutions later you hold eight Goblin tokens, and Impact Tremors has billed each opponent 8 damage (32 down to 24, 28 down to 20).

The not-cast clause then cuts the other way. Grapeshot, fired later as the fifth spell cast, sees a storm count of four and delivers five total instances of 1 damage — the storm copies earned it nothing. The holding: count your casts, not your resolutions.
combo_lines.003:
The controlling rule here is copy valuation: each Fists of Flame copy fixes its +1/+0-per-card-drawn value once, on its own resolution, and no later draw revises it retroactively. The facts, verified against the comprehensive rules (June 19, 2026 update): Zada and four Goblin tokens, one opponent at 30 life behind a lone untapped 2/2, two cards already drawn this turn, Fists of Flame cast for {1}{R} targeting only Zada. Her trigger makes four copies — not cast, so she doesn't re-trigger — and they resolve before the original, each drawing a card first, so the buffs lock in ascending: +3, +4, +5, +6 on the tokens, +7 on Zada herself. Five cards deeper, you are staring at 32 power of trample; the blocker absorbs at most 2, and at least 30 tramples through.

Exactly lethal — and exactness is why the checker refused to bless the line until the record walked the last step. Combat damage kills no one by itself: the game checks state-based actions before any player receives priority, finds a player at 0 or less life, and only then is the game over. When your math comes out exactly lethal, walk that step every time.
combo_lines.004:
A refutation — my favorite kind of holding, because the manual checks the database's homework. Commander Spellbook promises that Krenko, Mob Boss plus Skirk Prospector plus Goblin Warchief makes infinite tokens, infinite mana, and infinite storm; verified against the comprehensive rules (June 19, 2026 update), it does not — not in this deck. The claimed loop recasts Krenko through the command zone, and the rule that enables that, 903.9a, applies only to a commander — your commander is Zada, so a Krenko in the graveyard stays there. Nor can the loop turn over on the battlefield: his ability costs {T}, nothing here untaps him, and only untapped permanents can be tapped — one activation per turn, full stop.

What survives review is still excellent. With Warchief out, Krenko costs {1}{R}{R}, has haste, and taps immediately: on the example board of five Goblins, one activation makes five more — ten Goblins, thirteen power, all hasty, storm count a humble one. Skirk Prospector can then convert the seven spare tokens into seven one-shot red mana while keeping the whole engine (the mana empties at end of phase, so spend it now). Two standing orders: plan the turn around one activation, and never, ever sacrifice Krenko to Prospector — the rules have confirmed he does not come back.
combo_lines.005:
Affirmed in full: a verified true infinite, checked against the comprehensive rules (June 19, 2026 update). Two clauses carry the case: buyback returns only the original card to your hand — the storm copies cease to exist the moment they leave the stack — and Treasures are mana abilities, so nobody can respond to the payment. The facts: Storm-Kiln Artist, three Goblin tokens, four Mountains, three spells already cast, and Haze of Rage cast with buyback as the fourth; storm makes three copies, magecraft pays four Treasures, and every copy pumps the team +1/+0.

The engine math, verified: iteration k costs four mana and yields k+3 Treasures — net positive from cast three onward and strictly better every time. Two casts in, you hold Haze of Rage, own nine Treasures, and Storm-Kiln Artist is a 20/2. One note for the record: the loop itself touches no opponent, and your arbitrarily large team gains no haste or evasion from it. The kills are lines you assemble, not verified sequences — Fists of Flame for trample on a titan, the Treasure mana poured into Empty the Warrens under Impact Tremors, or a Grapeshot riding the storm count each real cast raised — so pick your exit before you start looping.

card_roles.Zada, Hedron Grinder: The whole operation. Any instant or sorcery cast targeting only Zada gets copied for each other creature you control, each copy at a different creature — a wide board turns your cantrips into mass draw. The combo graph pairs her with Storm-Kiln Artist; the synergy graph flags Frontline Heroism as her in-deck understudy.
card_roles.Crimson Wisps: The star of verified line 001. One red mana, targets only Zada, and the whole team turns red and hasty while you draw a card per creature — the best single spell in the deck on a wide board.
card_roles.Expedite: Same blueprint as Crimson Wisps: one target, haste, draw a card. Aimed only at Zada, it converts your board into cards and a surprise alpha strike.
card_roles.Renegade Tactics: A one-mana 'can't block' cantrip with a single target — that makes it Zada fuel. Mass evasion for the horde plus a card per creature.
card_roles.Ancestors' Aid: Pump plus a Treasure on a single-target instant, so it qualifies for Zada's trigger. On a big board it's a first-strike anthem and a mana injection at once.
card_roles.Fists of Flame: The go-tall payoff: draw a card, then the target gains trample and +1/+0 for each card you've drawn this turn. It targets one creature, so Zada's trigger applies — save it for the turn you've been drawing in bulk.
card_roles.Wild Ride: One-target haste and +3/+0 with a graveyard rebuy via harmonize — another spell built for Zada's 'targets only' requirement.
card_roles.Frontline Heroism: Zada's apprentice per the synergy graph (Copy + ETB): every spell you aim at a single creature you control mints a hasty Soldier and copies the spell onto it. Your target count snowballs.
card_roles.Dragon Fodder: Two Goblins for two mana. Bodies for Zada copies, Impact Tremors triggers, and sacrifice fodder — the simplest card in the deck and one of the most important.
card_roles.Krenko's Command: Dragon Fodder's twin: two more 1/1 Goblins, same job.
card_roles.Empty the Warrens: Storm token flood — every spell cast before it this turn makes another pair of Goblins. The natural crescendo of a ritual-and-cantrip chain.
card_roles.Mogg War Marshal: Three bodies stapled to one card — a token on entry, another on death. That's why the synergy graph rates him the deck's best sacrifice fodder (in-deck pairing with Goblin Trashmaster).
card_roles.Siege-Gang Commander: Three tokens on arrival, then a sac outlet that turns Goblins into 2-damage bolts. The synergy graph pairs him with Redcap Gutter-Dweller's token-and-sacrifice engine.
card_roles.Siege-Gang Lieutenant: Two hasty tokens every combat while your commander is out, plus a cheap sac-to-ping ability. The synergy graph pairs it with Redcap Gutter-Dweller as well.
card_roles.General Kreat, the Boltbringer: Attacking Goblins bring a friend, and every other creature that enters pings each opponent — a second Impact Tremors on legs. Combo graph partners: Goblin Bombardment, Goblin Chieftain, Goblin Warchief.
card_roles.Searslicer Goblin: Raid: a free Goblin every end step you attacked. Cheap, relentless board growth.
card_roles.Howlsquad Heavy: Haste for the tribe, a token every combat, and at max speed he taps for a red per Goblin — ritual and lord in one body. Combo graph partners: Krenko and Skirk Prospector.
card_roles.Redcap Gutter-Dweller: Two tokens on arrival, then an upkeep sacrifice that grows him and exiles a card you can play. The synergy graph's in-deck partner for both Siege-Gangs' sacrifice appetites.
card_roles.Impulsive Pilferer: Leaves a Treasure when it dies and Encores from the graveyard for three more bodies. Combo graph partners: Goblin Bombardment and Skullclamp — this card wants to die, so oblige it.
card_roles.Goblin Bushwhacker: Kicked, he gives the team +1/+0 and haste — the classic token-swarm finisher for the turn Empty the Warrens goes wide.
card_roles.Goblin Chieftain: Haste lord: other Goblins get +1/+1 and swing immediately. Combo graph partners: Krenko, General Kreat, Skirk Prospector.
card_roles.Goblin Warchief: Goblin spells cost less and everything hastes — half ramp, half lord. Combo graph partners: Krenko, General Kreat, Skirk Prospector.
card_roles.Goblin Trashmaster: A lord who eats Goblins to destroy artifacts. The synergy graph pairs him with Mogg War Marshal — sacrifice the token, keep the value.
card_roles.Rundvelt Hordemaster: Lord plus card-advantage engine: every Goblin death exiles a card, and Goblin creature cards among them can be cast. Board wipes become card flow. Combo graph partner: Skirk Prospector.
card_roles.Quest for the Goblin Lord: Five Goblin arrivals turn this one-mana enchantment into a permanent +2/+0 anthem. In this deck, five arrivals is a Tuesday.
card_roles.Goblin Lackey: Connect once and put any Goblin permanent from your hand straight onto the battlefield. A turn-one threat that demands an answer — let them spend one on it.
card_roles.Goblin Matron: Fetches whatever Goblin the moment calls for — Krenko for tokens, Skirk Prospector for mana, Bushwhacker for the kill.
card_roles.Gempalm Incinerator: Removal disguised as a Goblin: cycle it to deal damage to a creature equal to your Goblin count, and draw a card doing it.
card_roles.Goblin Dark-Dwellers: A menacing body that recasts a 3-or-less instant or sorcery from your graveyard for free — a second helping of Grapeshot, Faithless Looting, or a Zada cantrip.
card_roles.Grenzo, Havoc Raiser: Every creature that connects lets you goad a blocker or cast the top of an opponent's library. With a token horde, that's several triggers per combat.
card_roles.Broadside Bombardiers: A Boast sac outlet with menace and haste: trade a spare token or artifact for damage equal to 2 plus its mana value. The synergy graph places it squarely in the sacrifice cluster.
card_roles.Goblin Bombardment: The premier sacrifice outlet — every creature is a ping, no mana required. The combo graph's busiest hub: partners with Krenko, Impact Tremors, General Kreat, Impulsive Pilferer, Mana Geyser, Roaming Throne, and Sol Ring.
card_roles.Pashalik Mons: Every Goblin death becomes a damage ping, and he can eat a Goblin to make two more. With Bombardment out, your board is a machine gun. Combo graph partner: Skirk Prospector.
card_roles.Boggart Shenanigans: Quietly turns every Goblin funeral into a point of damage at any player or planeswalker. Pure reach for the attrition game.
card_roles.Skirk Prospector: Goblins are mana — verified in line 004 as a true mana ability: no stack, no responses, activatable mid-payment. On the example board he converts seven spare tokens into seven one-shot red mana (spend it before the phase ends). The combo graph's biggest hub with nine in-deck partners — but the rules say the Krenko pairing is a burst, not a loop, so feed him tokens, never the engine.
card_roles.Skullclamp: One mana turns any 1/1 token into two cards. In a token deck that's a card-advantage engine, and the combo graph pairs it with Impulsive Pilferer for extra credit.
card_roles.Battle Hymn: A ritual that scales with your board: add a red per creature you control. The setup spell for storm turns.
card_roles.Brightstone Ritual: A red for every Goblin on the battlefield — and it counts all Goblins, not just yours. Let the mirror pay your bill.
card_roles.Mana Geyser: Late in a turn cycle, opponents' tapped lands become a mountain of red mana. Combo graph partner: Goblin Bombardment.
card_roles.Seething Song: Three mana in, five out. Combo graph partners: Ruby Medallion and Storm-Kiln Artist — discounts and Treasures make it even better.
card_roles.Ruby Medallion: Every red spell costs one less, which in a deck of one- and two-mana spells effectively doubles your storm turn. Combo graph partners: Seething Song, Skirk Prospector.
card_roles.Sol Ring: Fast mana, no notes. Even the combo graph found it a partner here (Goblin Bombardment).
card_roles.Grapeshot: The storm kill: one damage per spell cast before it this turn, aimable anywhere. The payoff at the end of every ritual-and-cantrip chain.
card_roles.Haze of Rage: One half of the deck's verified infinite (line 005): buyback returns the card to hand every cast, storm multiplies it, and with Storm-Kiln Artist out each iteration mints more Treasures than the next cast costs — unbounded mana, storm count, and team pump. Even off-loop, it's a storm anthem. Combo graph partners: Storm-Kiln Artist and Throne of Eldraine.
card_roles.Spreading Insurrection: Storm Threaten: steal an untapped, hasty creature per copy. Turn the table's best boards against them on your combo turn.
card_roles.Storm-Kiln Artist: The paymaster and the other half of the verified infinite: a Treasure for every instant or sorcery you cast or copy — Zada copies and storm copies both count, as line 005 proves. Its +1/+0-per-artifact static means the loop also turns it into a giant (a 20/2 after just two Haze casts). Combo graph partners: Zada herself, Haze of Rage, and Seething Song.
card_roles.Past in Flames: The rebuild button: your whole graveyard of rituals and cantrips gains flashback for a turn. Cast your storm twice.
card_roles.Faithless Looting: Draw two, discard two, flashback later — smooths early hands and stocks the graveyard for Past in Flames and Dark-Dwellers.
card_roles.Glimpse the Impossible: Impulse three cards off the top; anything you don't use becomes Eldrazi Spawn tokens that sacrifice for mana. Card flow that leaves bodies behind.
card_roles.Witch's Mark: Loot away a dead card to draw two, and pin a Wicked Role on a creature so its eventual death stings each opponent.
card_roles.Idol of Oblivion: Tap for a card every turn you made a token. In this deck, that's nearly every turn.
card_roles.Great Train Heist: The modal haymaker: untap the team and take an extra combat, add first strike, or turn combat damage into Treasures — or all three on the turn that ends the game.
card_roles.Blasphemous Act: The reset: 13 damage to every creature, usually for one or two mana thanks to your own swarm. With Pashalik Mons or Boggart Shenanigans out, it's also a burn spell.
card_roles.Vandalblast: One-sided artifact sweeper via overload — the answer to Treasure decks and mana rocks that never touches your own Skullclamp.
card_roles.Swiftfoot Boots: Hexproof and haste for the creature everything revolves around. Boot up Zada before you commit to the big turn.
card_roles.Throne of Eldraine: Four red mana in one activation, or three mana and a tap for two cards. Mind the fine print: that mana casts spells only — it cannot pay an activated ability. Combo graph partner: Haze of Rage.
card_roles.Reliquary Tower: No maximum hand size — the card that lets a five-draw Zada turn actually stick.
card_roles.War Room: A land that draws cards for three mana and a life. Mono-red keeps the price low.
card_roles.Arena of Glory: Taps for one red normally, or exert it for two red that grants a creature spell haste — a ritual you replay every other turn.
card_roles.Castle Embereth: A pump land: +1/+0 to the team at instant speed. On twenty tokens, that's twenty extra damage.
card_roles.Den of the Bugbear: A creature-land that attacks as a 3/2 and brings a tapped, attacking Goblin token with it.
card_roles.Dwarven Mine: Enters untapped with three other Mountains and leaves a free 1/1 behind — a land that feeds the swarm.
card_roles.Kher Keep: Endless 0/1 Kobold tokens — cheap bodies for Zada targets and sacrifice outlets.
card_roles.Fountainport: Utility land that sacrifices spare tokens for cards, makes Fish chump-blockers, or mints Treasures.
card_roles.Goblin Burrows: +2/+0 to one Goblin per activation — spare-mana reach in the late game.
card_roles.Shinka, the Bloodsoaked Keep: First strike on demand for a legendary creature — Zada, Krenko, Kreat, or Grenzo swings safer.
card_roles.Spinerock Knoll: Hideaway: stash a spell, then cast it free once an opponent has taken 7 damage in a turn — a bar this deck clears constantly.
card_roles.Hidden Volcano: Late-game land that cashes in for Discover 4. A spare land becomes a spell.
card_roles.Forgotten Cave: A Mountain early, a card late — cycling smooths the draws.
card_roles.Smoldering Crater: Same deal as Forgotten Cave: land when you need it, card when you don't.
card_roles.Mountain: Twenty-two of them. Every one taps for exactly what the deck wants.
card_roles.Krenko, Mob Boss: Tap: double your Goblin count — a one-shot burst, and verified as exactly that in line 004. The database's 'infinite' Krenko/Prospector loop needs him in the command zone, and Zada holds that seat: a sacrificed Krenko is gone for good, and he stays tapped after one activation. Play him as five-plus tokens with haste under Warchief, and never sac him to Prospector.
card_roles.Impact Tremors: The quiet killer: one damage to each opponent for every creature that enters. An Empty the Warrens or a Krenko activation becomes a fireball to the whole table. Combo graph partner: Goblin Bombardment.
card_roles.Conspicuous Snoop: Casts Goblins off the top of your library and borrows the top Goblin card's activated abilities. Combo graph partner: Skirk Prospector.
card_roles.Roaming Throne: Name Goblin and every Goblin triggered ability triggers twice — Kreat, Pashalik Mons, Searslicer, Mogg War Marshal, all doubled. Ward 2 keeps it around. Combo graph partner: Goblin Bombardment.
card_roles.Moggcatcher: A repeatable Goblin tutor straight to the battlefield — four mana a turn buys whichever engine piece you're missing.
card_roles.Chaos Warp: Red's universal answer: shuffle away any permanent, from an enchantment you can't otherwise touch to a problem commander.
card_roles.Daring Discovery: Three attackers can't be blocked and Discover 4 finds you another spell — a pre-combat play that pushes damage and keeps the chain going.
card_roles.Goblin Negotiation: X-damage removal that pays you in Goblin tokens for excess damage. Removal that advances the plan.
card_roles.Sazacap's Brew: Sideboard flex, and not the Zada card it looks like: it targets a player, so it never "targets only Zada" and is never copied. What's left is a two-mana instant that discards as a cost to draw two — card-neutral selection plus one storm count. Don't test it in the Witch's Mark slot (Witch's Mark targets a creature and IS copyable); Spreading Insurrection is the slot, against a creature-light pod with no graveyard hate.

mulligan:
Keep hands that do two things: make Goblins early and cast spells cheaply. The gold standard is three lands — or two plus Sol Ring, Skirk Prospector, or Ruby Medallion — a one-or-two-mana token maker like Dragon Fodder, Krenko's Command, Mogg War Marshal, or Searslicer Goblin, and a cantrip like Crimson Wisps or Expedite banked for the turn Zada arrives. Zada is always waiting in the command zone at four mana, so your opener doesn't need a payoff. It needs bodies and mana.

Ship the hands that are all crescendo and no verse. Blasphemous Act, Mana Geyser, and Empty the Warrens with two lands is a mulligan — rituals and storm cards do nothing without a board and a spell count. Faithless Looting and Witch's Mark upgrade a marginal keep by trading dead cards for live ones.

One table tip from the corner office: the sideboard's Red Mana and Storm Counter cards are Secret Lair table aids with no rules text. Put them in front of you on big turns to track floating ritual mana and your storm count — a ten-spell turn is exactly when bookkeeping errors happen.

The goldfish numbers back the plan. Under the 2-to-5-land keep rule, 79% of first sevens are keepable, and the deck averages its first token maker by turn 3.2. A keep with bodies and cheap spells is the statistical default, not a gamble.
upgrades:
Ten names below, and only one is already in the building — the other nine are scouts from the pool, ranked by how directly they plug into the deck's three verified engines: Zada's copy-draw (stack 001), the Empty the Warrens storm burst under Impact Tremors (stack 002), and the Haze of Rage plus Storm-Kiln Artist loop (stack 005). That ranking is the whole methodology. A card that completes a line whose other pieces are already sleeved is worth more to this deck than a famous card that arrives alone.

Read the evidence tiers before you fall in love. Every combo line these ten open is flagged, not verified — a line becomes fact only when a stack artifact passes the checker, and each entry says so where it applies. The famous pool names that stayed off lost on an oracle read, not on reputation: Repercussion pairs with Blasphemous Act but turns the sweeper self-lethal under your own 1/1 swarm, and Glacial Chasm reads 'Creatures you control can't attack' in a deck that wins by attacking wide.

The one sideboard card that makes the cut, Sazacap's Brew, makes it on the narrowest possible grounds: it targets a player, so Zada never copies it. It earns the slot as storm fuel and card selection — one storm count plus a draw-two at instant speed — and nothing more. That honesty about what a card is not is exactly the standard the other nine were held to.
mana_base:
Thirty-six lands across 15 entries, 22 of them Mountains. Eight enter tapped — 22%, under the one-in-three budget. Mono-red keeps the colour ledger short: pip share and source share both sit at 1.0, so there is nothing to arbitrate and nothing to fix.

That leaves volume, and volume is fine. Thirty-three of the 36 lands make red, against a 90% yardstick that asks for 36 — the audit calls the target 'a yardstick, not a possibility' in a 36-land deck, yet lands alone already put red on curve 86.9% of the time. Three points off the mark before a single artifact enters the maths. The pips are cheap too: 69 red pips across 57 cards, and nothing in the list asks for more than {R}{R}.

So read the ramp column as burst, not as fixing. Rocks and dorks lift red to 43 sources and the on-curve figure to 96%, but that is not what six rituals are for. Rituals do not buy mana per turn; they buy mana in one turn, which is the only unit a storm count trades in. Battle Hymn and Brightstone Ritual scale with the board you already built, Skirk Prospector converts spare goblins on demand, and Storm-Kiln Artist mints Treasures off the very spells the mana is paying for.

The goldfish shows a normal, healthy curve and that is exactly the point. Land drops run 90.0% on turn 3 and thin to 54.2% by turn 6 — ordinary library maths — while mean available mana reads 3.937 on turn 4, 5.182 on turn 6, and 6.964 by turn 10. A mean of five or six mana never storms anybody out. The base's job is to deliver that five or six reliably; the rituals and the four dorks are how you beat the mean on the one turn you choose.

One line of fine print worth memorising: restricted mana counts for nothing in this audit, and Throne of Eldraine's red is spells-only — it cannot pay an activated ability. Don't earmark it for Goblin Burrows or Arena of Glory. Spend it on spells, where the storm count is watching.
threat_assessment:
The table reads your clock, so read it better. Zada, Hedron Grinder lands on turn 4 in 70% of games — 7,002 of 10,000 goldfish runs cast her exactly on 4 (mean 4.35, median 4, 90% by turn 6). Anyone who has seen this deck counts your Mountains and circles the turn-4 window. Good — let them stare at the window while you build behind it.

What they can't read is your board. On turn 3 you average just 2.36 bodies — a Skirk Prospector and a couple of 1/1 tokens look like chump blockers, not the fuel tank of a draw engine. That gap between what your board says and what your hand is building is your entire early game. Protect it.

The flip from ignored to archenemy happens at two exact thresholds, and you know both cold. One: Zada untapped, three-plus other creatures, one red mana open — verified stack 001 turns a single {R} Crimson Wisps into five cards and a hasted board. Two: the verified infinite.

Stack 005 proves Haze of Rage with buyback plus Storm-Kiln Artist goes mana-positive once about three spells have been cast that turn. Iteration k costs four mana and pays k+3 Treasures plus a team-wide +1/+0 — the loop strictly improves. In the verified run, two casts made 9 Treasures, three 10/1 Goblins, and a 20/2 Storm-Kiln.

So the moment Storm-Kiln Artist sits on your battlefield with four mana up and Haze in hand, informed opponents must respect lethal. Their counterplay is scripted: kill Storm-Kiln in response to the first magecraft trigger, or hit the Treasures with instant-speed artifact hate. Treat the first Haze cast as the commitment point. Fire when the table's interaction is tapped or spent — that's not caution, that's timing.

Your other tells are simple. Skullclamp screams engine deck. Conspicuous Snoop shows the table your library top all game. Price both in before you play them.

Sequencing under the radar is a script, and you own it. Deploy token makers early — Dragon Fodder and Krenko's Command read as defense, and the goldfish puts your early token maker at turn 3.18 on average, comfortably before Zada. Cast Zada as 'just a 3/3' and pass.

The full engine assembles at turn 5.27 on average and only 49.6% of the time by turn 6, so you usually get one quiet turn. Spend it wisely. Never fire a cantrip at Zada for two copies of value.

Know what Krenko, Mob Boss is here, because the table won't. The combo databases call Krenko plus Prospector plus a haste lord infinite; stack 004 verifies it is not a loop in this deck. Krenko is not your commander, he stays tapped after one activation, and a Krenko sacrificed to Prospector is simply gone.

Play him as a one-activation payoff: {1}{R}{R} under Warchief, five tokens on a modest board, ten Goblins and 13 hasted power. Never sacrifice him expecting recursion, and never burn protection defending a loop you don't have. When an opponent panic-removes Krenko expecting the Spellbook infinite, they've paid a real card for a one-shot — sometimes you let them.

Embrace being the threat only when the turn converts. Pace for the median game — the Zada draw engine plus wide pressure — and hold the ceiling as opportunism. The go-decision is arithmetic done before the first spell: count the mana and castable spells in your hand and on your board only; expected draws are a bonus, not a plan.

The go signs: Impact Tremors or Boggart Shenanigans down, Krenko untapped with his partners, a Spinerock Knoll set, or the Haze loop live. The goldfish assembles 'storm payoff plus ritual' in only 15.2% of games, so let the table's fear sit on cards you haven't drawn. The turn you draw five cards in front of three opponents, you are the archenemy — make it the turn the table has to answer you or start dying.
matchups:
Sweeper control (Azorius/Esper wraths): your engine is wrath insurance, not a wrath victim. Stack 001 proves one Crimson Wisps with four bodies banks five cards into a zone the sweeper can't touch, and Storm-Kiln Artist's magecraft mints Treasures that ride straight through a creature wrath — stack 005's 9 Treasures survive the board dying and fund the rebuild.

When the wrath is telegraphed at sorcery speed, change the arithmetic: go for value. Fire the cantrip engine and bank the draws instead of holding for a lethal that never gets cheaper. Hold one token maker in hand at all times and keep Past in Flames as your rebuild button. Pashalik Mons and Goblin Bombardment convert the wrath itself into a burst of damage on the way down, and Mogg War Marshal dies into another body.

Stax and tax pieces: taxes attack your velocity math, so recount your hand under the tax — a two-spell turn becoming a one-spell turn halves the engine. One lock piece is an inconvenience; the compounding second and third are the lock. You rarely own the long game here: you are the beatdown, racing the lock's assembly.

Name your outs early and by name — Vandalblast (overload {4}{R}), Goblin Trashmaster ('Sacrifice a Goblin: Destroy target artifact', repeatable), Chaos Warp for enchantments and commanders. Sequence to protect the one that breaks the piece that beats you, not the scariest piece.

Ruby Medallion and Goblin Warchief pay the toll, and Battle Hymn and Brightstone Ritual scale with your board rather than your lands — mana denial hurts less than the table assumes, since your land-drop rate falls to 54% by turn 6 anyway. Even the verified Haze loop survives a modest tax if you redo the math: iteration k yields k+3 Treasures against four mana plus the tax, so under a two-mana sphere the loop turns profitable a couple of casts later, not never.

Aggro and token mirrors: you win these on asymmetry, not size. Gempalm Incinerator cycles to kill their lord for X equal to all Goblins on the battlefield — theirs count too. Blasphemous Act is often {1}{R} in a token mirror; hold it as the reset you're uniquely built to rebuild from (mean 4.07 bodies by turn 5, rituals unmodeled).

Stack 004's verified burst is your mirror-breaker: Krenko for {1}{R}{R} under Warchief, one activation, ten Goblins and 13 hasted power from a three-body start — spend it as the one-shot it is. Anthems break stalls, and a single buyback Haze into a real storm count pumps your whole team past theirs. Impact Tremors plus General Kreat drain every opponent without ever attacking into blockers. Let the other token deck be the archenemy; you out-grind them.

Combo tables: your interaction is thin — Chaos Warp, Gempalm Incinerator, Bombardment as trigger-response — so held answers rot. Rank their combo proximity above every board threat and plan to disrupt once, cheaply, at the decisive moment.

Your own race line is real but narrow. Stack 005 verifies Haze of Rage plus Storm-Kiln Artist as a true infinite, and because every Haze cast is a real cast, the storm count climbs each iteration toward a Grapeshot payout. When you hold both pieces, do the go arithmetic before the first spell: three real casts before Haze makes the loop self-funding — count only hand and board.

Without the pieces, trust the goldfish: payoff-plus-ritual assembles in 15.2% of games, so your realistic clock is wide haste attacks plus Impact Tremors drain, with Grenzo goads pulling their defenses apart. Remember Zada's copies are not cast (rule 707.10) and add nothing to storm. If the table asks whether you're 'the storm deck', give the honest answer: a Goblin aggro deck with a very good draw engine — until Storm-Kiln Artist hits the battlefield.
